label: Bupivacaine — systemic disposition + site absorption

parameters.label: apparent volume of distribution (reference adult)
parameters.covariate_model: reference-adult disposition (no covariate model in LA0; ~1.0 L/kg)

extraction.tier_rationale: Standard reference-adult LA disposition value (Tier-C by design). Bupivacaine is long-acting and the most cardiotoxic common amide; the cardiotoxicity differentiation is v0.6 LA2.
extraction.source_locator: Tucker & Mather 1979; standard LA PK reference values

parameters.label: systemic clearance (reference adult)
parameters.covariate_model: reference-adult disposition (no covariate model in LA0)

extraction.source_locator: Tucker & Mather 1979; standard LA PK reference values

extraction.tier_rationale: Site-absorption rank order robust; absolute ka Tier-C, applied site-wise (the site dominates the rate of rise). The narrower cardiovascular margin of bupivacaine vs ropivacaine at similar block is the v0.6 LA2 educational comparison.
v0.6 LA0: systemic disposition + site absorption only — no toxicity thresholds (LA1). Site-of-injection dominance is the headline. Disposition + ka Tier-C; the site rank is the robust claim.
extraction.source_locator: Tucker & Mather 1979; standard LA PK reference values

notes: Systemic concentration only. Saturable protein binding (free fraction rises non-linearly at high total concentration) is curated on the drug record and surfaced as the LA3 failure mode; cardiotoxicity differentiation vs ropivacaine is LA2.
